_comment: STARTER TEMPLATE. Copy this whole folder to brands/<your-slug>/, then work top to bottom. Keys beginning with _comment are ignored by every part of the engine and exist only to explain the file. Delete them once you no longer need them. Do not put a _comment key inside 'palette' or inside any list of colours, marks or registers: those are read value by value and a comment string there fails verify. Every asset path below is relative to this folder and must be a real file before the render will run. See README.md for the file list and docs/PAGE-KINDS.md for every page kind and key.

meta._comment: slug MUST equal this folder's name. It names the output files, and verify looks for out/<folder>/<slug>-brand-presentation.pdf. If the two disagree, verify reports a missing PDF that is sitting right there.
meta.name: Your Business
meta.line: One sentence for the top of the board. Say the thing about this brand that is easiest to get wrong.

shape._comment: Only the three radii are safe to change. Leave margin, safeTop, gap, captionWidth, panelX, panelWidth and panelHeight out of this block entirely: they are one interlocking grid and the defaults are the ones that line up. docs/PAGE-KINDS.md explains the arithmetic.

type._comment: Any Google Fonts family name works. The first build fetches it and caches it into assets/fonts/ at the skill root, after which no network is needed. Set 'variable': true only for a face that really ships a weight axis. To use a licensed face instead, add "file": "assets/fonts/yourface.woff2" beside 'family'.

sections._comment: 'id' is not decoration. The brand board builds one card per section and looks the id up in a fixed list: overview, logo, colour, color, typography, imagery, motion, components, applications. A section with any other id still renders in the PDF and is silently absent from the board.
sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: What this business is, who it serves, and which parts of the brand are not written down yet.

pages.caption: Replace every block below with what is actually true. Where nothing has been decided, say so in the block rather than inventing a line that outlives the person who knew it was a guess.

blocks.title: What it is
blocks.body: One plain sentence naming the product or service and who buys it. No adjectives that could describe any competitor.

blocks.title: Who it is for
blocks.body: The specific buyer, described the way they would describe themselves. If two very different buyers are listed here, the brand is being asked to do two jobs.

blocks.title: How it should feel
blocks.body: Three words, chosen so that their opposites are also plausible brands. Words no business would ever refuse are not choices.

blocks.title: Voice and tagline
blocks.body: Not written yet. Nothing has been approved, so nothing is quoted here. Anything currently circulating as a tagline is a draft.

pages._comment: A 'prose' page is the brand's own hard rules. The emitted Claude skill lifts these verbatim, so write them as instructions a stranger could follow.
pages.caption: Short, testable, and about this brand specifically. A rule that applies to every brand on earth teaches nothing.
items: Never place the logo on a busy photograph. Use a flat ground or a scrim.
Never recolour the logo. Pick the variant that suits the ground instead.
One accent colour. Variety comes from photography, never from adding hexes.
Never stretch, rotate or add an effect to the artwork.

sections.title: Logo
sections.summary: The artwork, the grounds it is allowed to sit on, and the space it needs around it.

pages._comment: 'ground' picks the panel behind the artwork. Leave it out for the light card, or use 'dark' or 'accent'. A pale logo on a pale panel is invisible and correct, which is why the reversed lockup below asks for a dark ground.
pages.caption: The default everywhere. Say here what it is made of and where it is used.
For dark grounds. Say which grounds count as dark for this brand.
The symbol alone, for avatars, app icons and favicons. State the size below which the full lockup stops reading.

pages._comment: The measure is drawn to scale, not described. ratioValue is the padding as a fraction of markHeight; 'ratio' is only the label printed beside it. Keep the two in agreement.
pages.caption: A quarter of the logo height on every side. Nothing crosses it. No type, no graphic, no page edge.

sections.title: Colour
sections.summary: The grounds, the ink, and the one accent that carries every call to action.

pages._comment: These hexes are shown to the reader. They are not the same thing as the 'palette' block above, which colours the document itself. Keep them in step by hand.
pages.caption: Three colours do the work. Say what each one is for, not what it looks like.
Supporting values only. Nothing here is allowed to compete with the accent.

sections.title: Typography
sections.summary: One family, the weights that ship, and the size each role is actually set at.

pages._comment: Add an "axis" object here only for a variable face, for example "axis": {"min": 200, "max": 800, "steps": 7, "word": "Capability"}. On a static face it draws a ramp that is a lie.
pages.caption: Name the family and say what each weight is for. If two families are in use, add a second page like this one.

pages._comment: Every row is set at its true px value on the page, so a wrong number is visible rather than hidden. Tracking is negative and set per size.
pages.caption: Measure these off the real site or the real deck. A scale that was guessed is worse than no scale page at all.

sections.title: Applications
sections.summary: The system on real touchpoints, so the rules are seen working rather than described.

pages._comment: 'columns' is optional. Left out, it is 2 for four items or fewer and 3 above that. Each image fills its cell, so crop them to a similar aspect before dropping them in.
pages.caption: Real artefacts only. Every one of these should use the colours and the family already declared, and introduce nothing new.
